newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended down as fears of a United States interest rate rise swept global markets and knocked industrial shares firmly into negative territory, dealers said on Tuesday.
However, the golds index performed stronger, taking heart from a rally in the international bullion price that saw the local sector claw back more than half of Monday's steep losses.
"It was a quiet day. Everyone is waiting to see what happens in the United States," one dealer said.
The U.S. Federal Reserve is meeting to discuss whether a further rate rise is necessary to curb inflation fears in the country's booming economy.

Economic analysts are split as to the likelihood of a rise, but European equity markets and Wall Street shares headed downwards in the afternoon in anticipation of a hike and the South African market joined them.
The all-share index dropped 10.4 points to 7,106.2 as the industrial index dipped 26.5 points to 8,372.0. Volumes were modestly healthy as 611 million rands worth of shares changed hands.

The golds index climbed 20.3 points, or 1.7 percent, to 1,213.1 after losing nearly three percent on Monday. The index was boosted by bullion finding support above the key $340 an ounce level after looking dangerously close to breaking it.
It was another day when a relatively low level of underlying business was boosted by severl large individual deals.
Printing and publishing house, Nationale Pers Ltd, saw a 45 million rand asset swap between a local and offshore institution. The stock ended 10 cents off at 45.00 rand.

Amcoal ended down 100 cents to 304.00 rand after a single overseas buyer took stock worth 30 million rand and CGS Food Ltd was up 50 cents at 84.75 rand as another foreign investor bought 120,000 shares worth about 10 million rand in that firm.

Merger stories buoyed Lonrho Ltd shares to end up 20 cents at 10.50 rand and motor parts firm Chariot Ltd's confirmation of the long-rumoured buy of a Federal Mogul SA unit saw the firm drop five cents to 112 cents on profit-taking.
Industrial holding firm Barlow Ltd dropped 200 cents to 46.85 rand as the market continued to adjust the firm's valuation in the wake of poor results on Monday.
Dealers said the market's direction on Wednesday would be firmly directed by the Federal Reserve's rate decision and the corresponding global market reaction.
But some dealers thought a hike was already discounted in the local market's valuation and sentiment was more likely to follow the bullion price.
"The market is perhaps moving on the back of bullion... a rate rise should not have any real impact on us," said Dominic Rey, a dealer at Investec.

Near-dated futures also weakened after a firm start to the day as players began to accept a U.S. rate rise as likely. But the gold contracts had a strong day and dealers said they were set to continue up on Wednesday.
The all-share June contract was at 6,538/40 from 6,533 as the industrials contract was last at 8,183/90 from 8,188. The golds contract was at 854/65 from 827.
